title: Three Moments From One Event, and What Each One Did
slot: Art · Trinity Arts Award Silver Unit 1
objective: Review one arts event from the approved event pack, writing three moments, each naming the craft choice, the audience it acted on and the effect it had.

blocks.text: LAUNCH · Art · Week 6. Trinity Arts Award Silver Unit 1. Three Moments From One Event, and What Each One Did.
Objective: review one arts event from the approved event pack, writing three moments, each naming the craft choice, the audience it acted on and the effect it had.
Success evidence: three moment entries, each with a named craft choice, a named audience and an effect, plus one verdict sentence and your attendance evidence attached.
Everything you describe comes from the approved event pack and your event record sheet. You are not asked about your home, your family or your own days out. You review the event, not your life.
40 minutes. Offline.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve
stages.data-ta1: Event pack and record sheet out before the frame. Check every pupil has a dated attendance item in front of them.
stages.data-ta2: If a pupil starts describing a family trip or a night at home, name the event pack in front of them and move on. Do not follow it up.

blocks.text: Being there is only half the evidence
An arts event is a public arts offer you attended: a performance, an exhibition, a screening or a workshop.
The assessor needs two separate things from you.
The first is attendance evidence: a ticket, a programme, a listing or a dated photograph.
The second is response evidence: what you noticed in the room, and what it did.
Attendance evidence on its own proves you were there. It proves nothing about your response.
Response evidence on its own could be written by somebody who never went.
Today you build the second, and attach it to the first.
Both halves go in the folder together. A review with no ticket, listing or programme behind it cannot be signed off.
You need three things on the desk. The event pack. Your event record sheet. The review frame.

stages.title: Starter · create the need
stages.data-ta1: Both accounts face up at the same time. Do not say which one is better before the group has read them.

blocks.text: Two accounts of the same event
Read account A. It walks through the evening in order, from arriving to leaving.
It is long, it is accurate, and it earns almost nothing.
Read account B. It picks three moments and then stops.
It is shorter, and it is the one that gets marked.
A recount tells the assessor what happened. A review tells them what the makers chose, and what that choice did.
Order is easy to write, so most people write order. Choices are what the mark scheme asks for.

items: 2 · name the choice the maker made.
3 · say who it acted on, and what it did.
4 · give a verdict you can defend.

stages.title: I Do · model
stages.data-ta1: Model one moment only, then stop. Do not offer a second example even if the group asks for one.

blocks.text: One moment, worked all the way through
I take the last two minutes of the performance in the event pack.
That is my moment. It has a place and a time, so it can be checked.
Now the choice. The lighting designer cut the whole stage down to one lamp.
Lighting is a craft term. Craft terms are the words the assessor is looking for.
Now the effect. The audience around me stopped shifting, and the room went quiet.
Now the verdict. It worked, because the ending felt small and close instead of grand.

blocks.caption: Skip a box and the next one has nothing to stand on
blocks.title: One moment, worked through
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows: the moment, the craft choice, the effect on people, the verdict

blocks.text: I did not write that the show was amazing. Amazing gives nobody anything to check.
Craft terms you may use today: lighting, framing, scale, palette, tempo, staging, sound and materials.
Say each of the four labels aloud as you write it. The labels are the thing being taught, not the show.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits
stages.data-ta1: Cards sorted first, matched second. Nobody speaks until every pupil has a hand on a card.

blocks.text: Sort the cards, then match them
Eight cards are face up on your table. Each is a line from a real review.
Sort the eight cards into two groups: moments and recounts.
A moment holds a place or a time. A recount only holds an order.
Then match each moment card to the craft choice it names: lighting, tempo, scale or palette.
Every person puts a hand on one card before anybody speaks.
Two cards are hard on purpose. They carry a time and still name no choice, so they are recounts.
When your table has finished, hold up the card you argued about longest.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect
stages.data-ta1: Audience list from the event pack face up beside the frame. Verdicts are written against that list, not from memory.

blocks.text: A verdict has to name its audience
A verdict with no audience is an opinion, and an opinion cannot be checked.
Good is not a verdict. Good for whom, and doing what, is a verdict.
The event pack names four audiences: the school group, the family audience, first-time visitors and people who already know the work.
My verdict was that the single lamp worked. Now I say who for.
It worked for first-time visitors, because it left them nothing else to look at.

blocks.caption: The same number of words, and only one of them is evidence
blocks.title: Named audience against general praise
blocks.alt: Two boxes side by side: a verdict that names its audience, and a verdict that is only an adjective

blocks.text: The same choice can fail a different audience. One lamp may have lost the people at the back, and a strong review says so.
Last comes influence. Name one thing this event changes about your own Unit 1 plan.

items: 2 · name the audience it is about.
3 · say what that audience did or felt.
4 · name one change to your own plan.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab
stages.data-ta1: Pair by table, not by choice. Two and a half minutes each way, timed out loud.

blocks.text: Two questions on your partner's moment
Work in twos. Swap sheets and read one of your partner's moments in silence.
Then ask two questions, in this order. Which choice? Which audience?
If they cannot answer the first, ring the moment and write choice missing.
If they cannot answer the second, write audience missing instead.
You are not saying the moment is bad. You are saying which box is still empty.
Then swap back and fix only the box that was ringed.
One word is banned in this task. Good, unless the next word is for.

stages.title: Independent · evidence
stages.data-ta1: Scribe the pupil's exact words. Do not supply the craft term they left out; mark that box empty instead.
stages.data-ta2: A pupil who can only find two moments keeps two, and writes one line saying why the third is missing.

blocks.text: Three moments and one verdict
Work on your own. Fill the record sheet from the event pack.
Write three moments. Each one needs a place or a time, a craft choice and an effect.
Write the effect as something people did or felt, not as a word for the whole event.
Then write one verdict sentence underneath, and name the audience it is about.
Then attach your attendance evidence, and write what it is: ticket, programme, listing or photograph.
Last, write one line saying what this event changes about your own plan.
If you finish early, swap the craft term in your weakest moment for a sharper one.

items: Supported · two moments, each naming a craft choice, and one verdict.
Standard · three moments, each with a choice and an effect, plus a verdict naming its audience.
Stretch · as Standard, and name one audience the same choice may have failed.

stages.title: Exit · Audience and Influence
stages.data-ta1: The named adult reads it back word for word and names the audience they heard. No paraphrase.

blocks.text: Read one moment to an adult
Read one moment and your verdict to the adult at your table.
They read it back, and tell you which audience they heard in it.
If they heard none, add the audience now, in three words or fewer.
Then choose what happens next: file it, add the third moment, or book the next event.
Write that choice and today's date on the sheet before you leave.
The sheet and the attendance evidence go into the arts log folder together.

sections: The verdict and who it is for
print.intro: Fill one moment box at a time. Leave a box empty rather than filling it with something you did not see.

One verdict sentence that names the audience it is about
tiers: Write two moments, each naming a craft choice, and one verdict.

checks: Three moments each carry a place or a time from the approved event pack.
Each moment names a craft choice, not an adjective.
The verdict names the audience it is about.
Attendance evidence is attached and named on the sheet.
